trials.hypothesis: Raise gamma from 0.95 to 0.99 and gae_lambda from 0.9 to 0.95. The +1 exact-build bonus comes 8 to 20 placements after early choices. """Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting recipe's 4 seeds were bimodal (0.068 three times, 0.258 once), so seed luck dominates. A 2-seed mean can move by about ±0.1 by chance alone. The default budget is 131k steps, or only 32 PPO updates of 4,096 samples each, which is very few. Probable bottlenecks: (1) too few updates or samples, since cutting PPO epochs buys more samples; (2) gamma 0.95 discounts the +1 exact-build bonus heavily over episodes of 8 to 20 placements, while exact completion and timing DONE are what success measures; (3) the batches are large relative to the number of updates. Round 1 tests three separate levers, each with one main change, to find out which direction moves dev success: longer credit horizon, more samples per FLOP, and more frequent updates.
analyses.2: All three recipe changes landed at 0.0674 to 0.0684. That is the same value as three of the starting architecture's four seeds (0.068). So 0.068 looks like a common plateau, probably a fixed greedy behaviour that only builds the simplest designs exactly. The one seed that escaped reached 0.258. None of the changes made escape more likely, but none hurt either. Training is very short (about 42 s against a 900 s limit), and success on training episodes stays at 4 to 7%, so the agent is undertrained. Cutting PPO epochs to 2 gave 1.8x more samples and slightly higher training success (0.065), which hints that more data helps. Next I test three levers that could break the plateau: still more samples with a stronger step size (1 epoch, higher lr), a higher lr on top of the current best, and less entropy. The entropy bonus over about 401 actions may keep the policy too diffuse, when exact builds need precise, irreversible placements.
analyses.3: Six recipe changes have all landed on exactly 0.0684 for every seed. That is the same score as three of the four baseline seeds (35 of 512 dev designs). So 0.0684 is a stable mode that runs fall into, not seed noise. Training success also stays near 0.07. Only one baseline seed escaped, to 0.258. Using fewer epochs to get more samples, a higher learning rate, smaller batches, a longer horizon alone, or lower entropy did not move runs out of this mode. The remaining levers look like exploration (more entropy), combining long-horizon credit with many more samples and longer rollouts, and the opposite of what has been tried so far: heavier sample reuse with more PPO epochs. The only breakthrough happened at 4 epochs, so reuse may matter.
analyses.4: Nearly every run ends at exactly 0.0684. This looks like a stable local optimum, most likely the agent builds only the easiest designs exactly. Only two seeds have escaped it: the baseline with 4 epochs (0.258) and r3c1 with ppo_epochs 2 and ent_coef 0.03 (0.213). Changing gamma, lambda, batch size or learning rate, using fewer epochs or more samples, and lowering entropy all stayed at 0.0684. Eight epochs collapsed to 0. The only lever that has moved the result so far is more entropy, which keeps exploring long enough to reach the exact-build bonus on harder designs. One escaped seed out of two is still within noise. This is the last round, and the top 3 trials get more seeds, so all three candidates vary around high entropy. Each one varies a single axis: more entropy, more sample reuse, or more samples.
